Think of a kitchen where the cook plates food faster than the waiter can carry it. Plates pile up until the waiter calls back to slow down. That call back is backpressure: the part that receives work tells the part that sends it to ease off.

What it's actually doing: a message queue holds messages until a consumer takes them, and when the consumer falls behind, the queue makes the sender wait or refuse new messages instead of growing forever.
